title: Please stop treating high blood pressure as a mistake
body:
Overall, the Health app is great — it’s useful that you can track many different metrics, and that can genuinely help people monitor their wellbeing.
However, the blood pressure tracking experience is very frustrating.
	1.	If someone doesn’t have blood pressure issues, they probably won’t use this feature. But if they do have issues, the app repeatedly warns them every single time they enter a reading (“your values are too high”, “make sure you didn’t enter it wrong”). When you’re recording real measurements, this feels like constant distrust and becomes annoying. Please make this warning optional — for example, add a toggle like “I understand, don’t show this again”.
	2.	Data entry is awkward: the systolic field allows more than three digits, which makes no sense. A well-designed UI would automatically move the cursor to the next field after three digits. Right now you have to tap into the next field manually and then confirm the input every time.

Please improve this section by making warnings dismissible/optional and fixing the input flow (3-digit limit and auto-advance between fields). This would greatly improve the experience for people who rely on this feature regularly.

title: Sleep and water trackings.
body:
I never thought I would give a one-star rating to an Apple app.
I had a Garmin watch for $250 that perfectly tracked my sleep as soon as I turned on sleep mode. But I still switched to the Apple Watch Ultra 2 since all my devices are from Apple. I decided to sacrifice battery life for an Apple watch.
But a watch that costs $1050 (price in Norway) doesn't have a built-in water tracker, so I have to use a third-party app. Apple, are you serious???

Why can't I track my sleep if I sleep two or three times a day?

Or why can't I set different schedules?

For example, my schedule changes every week. Sometimes I work at night and sometimes during the day.
I went to sleep after a night shift, turned on sleep mode, had to manually change the schedule. And guess what, my watch didn't track my sleep. How is that even possible? Even with sleep mode on, my watch didn't understand it needed to work. Terrible!!!! Apple, do something about it!
